en: To attack violently, physically or with criticism
hook: ASSAIL: ASSAULT someone.
story: Critics assailed the new movie as racist and lazy. Doubts assailed Nadia the night before her exam: was she really ready? To assail is to attack fiercely, with blows, words, or worries. Synonyms: assault, attack, impugn.

en: Well-meaning and kind; charitable
hook: BENE-VOLENT: wishing (vol) good (bene).
story: The benevolent old man fed every stray dog on his street and paid school fees for his maid's children. Benevolent means kind and generous. A benevolent fund helps people in need. The opposite is malevolent.

en: To scold or criticize angrily
hook: BE-RATE: give someone a terrible RATING, loudly.
story: The bus conductor berated a passenger for not having change, shouting at him in front of everyone. To berate is to scold angrily at length. Synonyms: upbraid, chastise, castigate.

en: Able to float; cheerful and optimistic
hook: BUOYANT: like a BUOY, always floating up.
story: After passing all his exams, Tanvir was in a buoyant mood, smiling at everyone and humming songs. A life jacket is buoyant; so is a growing economy. Buoyant means able to float, or cheerful and resilient.

en: To support or strengthen
hook: BUTTRESS: the stone supports holding up a cathedral wall.
story: Mitu buttressed her argument with statistics, expert quotes, and real-life examples. Her professor couldn't find a weak point. To buttress is to reinforce, like stone buttresses supporting old church walls. Synonym: bolster.

en: To accept or overlook wrong behavior
hook: CONDONE: CON + DONE, letting a con be done without objection.
story: The teacher saw a student copying but said nothing. By staying silent, she condoned the cheating. To condone is to accept or allow behavior that is wrong. A society that condones corruption gets more of it.

en: To violate a law or rule
hook: CONTRA-VENE: come (vene) AGAINST (contra) the rule.
story: Building a factory on the riverbank contravened environmental laws, and the court ordered it shut. To contravene is to violate or break a law. Synonyms: breach, infringe, transgress.

en: To publicly declare something wrong or evil
hook: DE-NOUNCE: ANNOUNCE it's bad.
story: World leaders denounced the attack on civilians, calling it a crime against humanity. To denounce is to publicly condemn. You can also denounce a person to the authorities, informing on them.

en: Ruling with absolute and often cruel power
hook: DESPOTIC: a DESPOT, an all-powerful tyrant.
story: The despotic king jailed anyone who criticized him, controlled every newspaper, and taxed the poor to build his palaces. Despotic means tyrannical. A despot rules with absolute power. Synonyms: autocratic, dictatorial.

en: To depart from an established course or norm
hook: DE-VIA-TE: off the road (via).
story: The bus driver deviated from the usual route to avoid a protest, taking a long detour through narrow lanes. Arif never deviates from his morning routine. To deviate is to depart from the usual path. Synonyms: diverge, stray.

en: Impartial; not influenced by personal advantage
hook: GRE trick: DISINTERESTED = no personal INTEREST (stake). Not the same as uninterested!
story: To settle the land dispute, both families chose a disinterested judge, someone with no connection to either side and nothing to gain. Disinterested means impartial and unbiased. It doesn't mean bored; that's uninterested.

en: To increase rapidly in intensity or seriousness
hook: ESCALATE: like an ESCALATOR, going up and up.
story: What began as an argument over a parking spot escalated into shouting, then shoving, then a full fight involving twenty people. To escalate is to rapidly increase in intensity. Prices escalate, conflicts escalate.

en: To drive out an evil spirit; to get rid of something troubling
hook: EXORCISE: EXIT the demons.
story: In the old village story, the ojha exorcised the ghost from the haunted banyan tree. Years later, Mitu tried to exorcise the painful memory of her failed exam by succeeding on her second try. To exorcise is to drive out something evil or troubling.

en: Fussy and hard to please; requiring great attention to detail
hook: FINICKY: FINE details only — picky.
story: The finicky cat refused any food except one brand of fish, served at exactly room temperature in a blue bowl. Finicky means fussy and hard to please. A finicky machine needs constant adjustment. Synonym: fastidious.

en: To prevent something from succeeding; a person who contrasts with another
hook: FOIL: wrap the plan in FOIL so it can't work.
story: The guard's quick action foiled the robbery; he locked the gate and called the police before the thieves could escape. To foil is to thwart. As a noun, a foil is a character who contrasts with another, like a calm friend beside a hot-tempered hero.

en: Twisted together; closely connected
hook: INTER-TWINED: TWINE twisted together.
story: The roots of the two old trees had grown intertwined over a hundred years; you couldn't tell where one ended and the other began. Bangladesh's history is intertwined with its rivers. Intertwined means closely linked or twisted together.

en: To flood; to overwhelm with too much of something
hook: INUNDATE: IN + UNDA (wave). Waves pour in.
story: The monsoon floods inundated half the district. After her viral video, Sara was inundated with messages: thousands of them in one day. To inundate is to flood, literally or figuratively. Synonyms: deluge, swamp, overwhelm.

en: Impossible to break or contradict
hook: IRON-CLAD: covered in IRON armor.
story: The lawyer drafted an ironclad contract with no loopholes. The suspect had an ironclad alibi: he was on live TV at the time of the crime. Ironclad means unbreakable and secure, like old warships covered with iron.

en: To put someone or something in danger
hook: JEOPARDIZE: put it in JEOPARDY.
story: Arif's habit of skipping classes jeopardized his scholarship; one more absence and he would lose it. To jeopardize is to put at risk. Texting while driving jeopardizes lives. Synonyms: endanger, imperil.

en: Subject to sudden, unpredictable changes of mood
hook: MERCURIAL: like MERCURY (liquid metal), never stays still.
story: The director was mercurial: laughing and hugging the crew one minute, screaming and throwing scripts the next. Nobody knew which version would arrive each morning. Mercurial means unpredictably changeable. Synonyms: capricious, volatile.

en: Not aware of what is happening around one
hook: OBLIVIOUS: in OBLIVION, totally unaware.
story: Wearing headphones and staring at his phone, Tanvir was oblivious to the rickshaw heading straight for him until someone pulled him back. Oblivious means completely unaware. Many people are oblivious to their own bad habits.

en: To carry out a harmful, illegal, or immoral act
hook: PERPETRATE: a PERP (criminal) does it.
story: The gang perpetrated a series of bank frauds over five years before finally being caught. To perpetrate is to commit a crime or harmful act. The perpetrator is the person who did it. Don't confuse it with perpetuate, which means to make something continue.

en: Sounding sad and mournful
hook: PLAINTIVE: like a PLAINT, a sad complaint.
story: From across the river came the plaintive sound of a boatman's song, a slow melody about a lost love. Everyone on the bank fell silent. Plaintive means sad and mournful. A puppy's plaintive whimper melts every heart.

en: Evoking a keen sense of sadness or deep emotion
hook: POIGNANT: POINTED, it pierces your heart.
story: The final scene, an old mother waiting at the train station for a son who would never return, was so poignant that the whole theater cried. Poignant means deeply moving, especially in a sad way. A poignant memory touches your heart sharply.

en: In a state of inactivity or dormancy
hook: QUIESCENT: QUIET and resting.
story: The volcano had been quiescent for three hundred years, until one morning it rumbled back to life. The disease can stay quiescent in the body for years before symptoms appear. Quiescent means inactive or dormant, at rest.

en: To say something again, often for emphasis
hook: RE-ITERATE: say it again and again (iterate).
story: 'I'll reiterate,' the doctor said firmly. 'Take this medicine every day, even if you feel better.' She repeated it three times so nobody would forget. To reiterate is to repeat for emphasis.

en: To become less intense, violent, or severe
hook: SUB-SIDE: sinking down (sub) to the side.
story: After three days, the floodwaters finally began to subside, revealing muddy roads and damaged homes. Rafi's anger subsided once he heard his friend's explanation. To subside is to calm down or decrease. Synonym: abate.

en: To include or absorb something into a larger category
hook: SUB-SUME: SUM it UNDER a larger heading.
story: When the two small departments were subsumed into the larger Ministry of Education, their names disappeared from the org chart. To subsume is to include within something larger. Apples and mangoes are subsumed under the category of fruit.

en: To overcome a difficulty or obstacle
hook: SUR-MOUNT: climb OVER the MOUNTain.
story: Born without the use of his legs, the athlete surmounted every obstacle to win a Paralympic medal. To surmount is to overcome a difficulty, like climbing over a mountain. Insurmountable problems are ones that can't be overcome.

en: Only slightly related; diverging from the main topic
hook: TANGENTIAL: like a TANGENT line, it only touches the circle at one point.
story: Asked about rising fuel prices, the spokesman gave a tangential answer about solar panels in Germany. It barely touched the question. Tangential means only slightly connected. Going off on a tangent means drifting away from the topic.
